relationships.evidence_quote: We found that hIFN-α and hIFN-β induced a concentration-dependent increase in the phosphorylation of STAT1 (Tyr701) in the nuclear compartment of peripherin-positive neurons 1 hour after treatment (Figure 4, A–D), suggesting early canonical downstream signaling induced by direct stimulation of IFNRs.

relationships.subject: type I IFNs
relationships.evidence_quote: A dose of 500 U/mL of both IFNs increased the phosphorylation of eIF4E (serine 209), a specific biochemical target of MNK1/2 (56) (Figure 6).

relationships.subject: type I IFNs
relationships.evidence_quote: Together these results demonstrate that type I IFNs promote hyperexcitability over short (up to 1 hour) and long (24–48 hours) times in most hDRG neurons.

relationships.subject: type I IFNs
relationships.evidence_quote: These results agree with MEA findings, showing that TRPV1 activity is modulated by type I IFNs in hDRG neurons.

relationships.subject: eFT508
relationships.evidence_quote: Further, an increased AP spike rate in response to capsaicin application was observed with both hIFN-α and hIFN-β, and this effect was abrogated by preincubation with eFT508 (Figure 7, C and D).

key_findings: Human DRG nociceptors express IFNAR1 and IFNAR2; type I IFNs induce STAT1 and MNK1/2-eIF4E signaling and acute and long-term hyperexcitability.
Type I IFNs sensitize TRPV1 responses to capsaicin in human DRG neurons, and the MNK1/2 inhibitor eFT508 blocks this effect.
